name: Dennis Koshta
shortBio: I build LLM systems, AI tools, and interactive projects. I’m especially interested in AI safety and alignment.
aboutParagraphs: I’m Dennis, a software engineer based in San Francisco. I work at Bronco AI, where I build tools and evaluation systems for AI agents. Outside work, I spend a lot of time building and experimenting with my own projects.

AI safety and alignment are particular interests of mine. I want to understand how models behave, whether we can trust the ways we test them, and how to keep increasingly capable systems under human control. Some of my projects explore these questions through training experiments, formal verification, and model internals.

I also enjoy the practical side of LLM systems: getting agents, tools, and the software around them to work well together. And I like making things just because they’re interesting—games, music tools, simulations, websites, or an idea I want to try out.

experience.description: Building agent evaluation systems, document-review tools, and knowledge-base infrastructure.
Worked on retrieval and LLM integrations for a SaaS platform, along with authorization and backend infrastructure.
Led a four-person team working on reinforcement learning and LLM agents, including a Minecraft agent that could gather resources and craft items.
Co-founded an AI analytics platform and worked on product direction, full-stack development, and its private beta.

experience.role: Machine Learning and Data Teams Lead · Project Manager
experience.description: Led ML and data work on a project that classified subvocal phonemes from muscle signals, including the experiment and training pipelines.

education.description: B.S. in Computer Science and B.S. in Mathematics Theory and Computation, with a minor in Statistics. Graduated in 2025.

collaborationParagraphs: I use Codex and Claude Code for coding, experiments, and review. I choose what to build, test the results, and decide what to keep. The project pages explain my role and credit collaborators.
The interactive projects are collaborations with GPT and Claude. For the research experiments, I include methods, results, and limitations so you can see what was actually tested.

interestsParagraphs: My interests go well beyond CS and AI. I like learning about math, biology, and physics, including quantum physics. I don’t need a project in mind to find a subject worth exploring.
Away from the computer, I’m into prog rock, cooking, and backpacking.
